name: Kobo
description: Canadian e-book and e-reader company (a Rakuten subsidiary) selling eBooks, audiobooks, Kobo eReaders and accessories through kobo.com in Canada, the US, the UK, Australia and the EU.

evidence.summary: Kobo's own Writing Life Help Centre page states Kobo has partnered with Rakuten Advertising for its affiliate program: KWL author rates of 6% on eBooks & audiobooks, 5% on Kobo devices, 10% on accessories, 5% on gift cards, plus $1 per new customer and $1 per Kobo Plus subscription, with a 14-day cookie; free to join.

The same official page's FAQ asks 'Is there a limit on the amount of commission I can make?' and answers 'There are no limits on how much commission you can make!' — an explicit no-cap statement, so the commission cap is recorded as uncapped.

Geniuslink's program write-up states the general (non-author) Kobo program on Rakuten Advertising pays 5% on ebooks, audiobooks and device purchases and 10% on device accessories, with a 14-day cookie; the recorded rate is the 5% headline general rate.

reasons.niche_fit: eReaders, eBooks and audiobooks are natural review and reading-routine content for tech and book creators.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program is promoted on Kobo's own Writing Life channel and explicitly welcomes authors, publishers, bloggers and influencers as affiliates.
reasons.compensation: 5% headline general rate (10% accessories, $1 bounties on the author rate card) with a verified no-cap statement on the brand's own page; short 14-day cookie tempers the score.
reasons.contact_access: No public affiliate email; application runs through Rakuten Advertising sign-up as documented on the brand's help page.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open, free application through Rakuten Advertising across five regional programs (US, Canada, EU, Brazil, Australia).
reasons.credibility: Major global e-reading brand owned by Rakuten, running its affiliate program on Rakuten Advertising since 2011.

name: Krisp
description: AI voice-clarity software company whose app removes background noise and adds meeting assistance for calls, sold as a subscription to individuals, remote workers, creators and teams.

evidence.summary: Krisp's own partners page runs three tracks — Affiliate, Creator and Co-marketing. The Affiliate track pays 30% recurring commission for 12 months with a 90-day cookie, and its 'Join the program' button routes to Impact; the Creator track (custom terms) routes to a Dub partners page.

The page's FAQ asks 'Does Krisp have an affiliate program, and how much can I earn?' and answers that the program pays 30% recurring for 12 months and 'there's no cap on what you can earn' — an explicit no-cap statement from the brand, so the cap is recorded as uncapped.

The page explicitly invites influencers and creators (including beginners), offers an asset and swipe-copy library, monthly creative drops and partner office hours, and says audience size matters less than how and where the partner will promote.

reasons.niche_fit: A call-noise tool is highly demonstrable in creator, streaming, podcast and remote-work content.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand's own page has a dedicated Creator track plus an affiliate track, with creative assets and monthly drops built for content partners.
reasons.compensation: 30% recurring for 12 months with a 90-day cookie and a verified no-cap statement on the brand's own page — the strongest pay terms in this group.
reasons.contact_access: Application forms for each track are on the brand's own partners page, with a partner Slack and office hours after joining; no public email published.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application, free to join, beginners explicitly welcome; applications reviewed in 2–3 working days.
reasons.credibility: Established voice-AI company (Forbes AI 50, Webby winner) with named enterprise customers on the page.

name: BullyBillows
description: UK-based premium dog gear brand designing heavy-duty harnesses, Combat collars and leads for strong and bully breeds, developed and tested with Nottingham Trent University and sold worldwide.

evidence.summary: The brand's own Awin programme profile lists as its first reason to promote: 'A competitive commission structure with uncapped earning potential', plus exclusive partnership opportunities and dedicated affiliate management. No percentage rate is published on the profile, so the rate is recorded as null.
'Uncapped earning potential' on the brand's own network listing is an explicit statement that earnings are not capped, so the commission cap is recorded as uncapped.

UK harness guide Smart Bark describes BullyBillows as a UK-based brand collaborating with Nottingham Trent University on harness design and testing; the brand's own store states over 1 million products sold.

reasons.niche_fit: Heavy-duty harnesses and collars for strong breeds are extremely demonstrable in dog-training and big-dog content.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The Awin profile offers exclusive partnerships, competitions and voucher codes, and the brand is built on influencer-led social reach.
reasons.compensation: Verified uncapped earning potential on the brand's own Awin listing, but no published percentage rate, which holds the score down.
reasons.contact_access: No public email on the profile; contact runs through the Awin programme's affiliate management.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open to publishers through Awin with dedicated affiliate management advertised.
reasons.credibility: Established UK pet brand with 1M+ products sold and a university testing collaboration.

name: Backblaze
description: US cloud storage and computer backup company; its consumer Computer Backup service is an unlimited-backup subscription for Mac and PC, sold alongside B2 cloud storage.

evidence.summary: Backblaze's own blog announcement of its Partner Program states that Affiliates 'can enjoy recurring 10% commissions' on computer backup, alongside channel, technology and MSP partner tracks, with sign-up through its Partner page.

Lasso's program listing confirms 10% recurring commission with a 30-day cookie; Backblaze's own partner guidance states affiliates earn 10% of the purchase price for the lifetime of each Computer Backup license (B2 cloud storage excluded), paid via PayPal at a $100 threshold.
No earnings-cap statement appears in the brand's program materials, so the commission cap is recorded as unknown.

reasons.niche_fit: Backup software fits tech, productivity and creator-workflow content, though it is less visual than hardware.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The affiliate track sits inside a general partner program aimed mainly at businesses and MSPs; no creator-specific recruitment was found.
reasons.compensation: 10% recurring for the lifetime of each referred Computer Backup license — genuine recurring revenue; no cap statement, so cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: A partner portal and partner page are published on the brand's own site; no public affiliate email was published.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open affiliate track within the brand's own Partner Program.
reasons.credibility: Publicly traded, long-established US cloud storage company (Nasdaq: BLZE).

name: Mobile Pixels
description: US portable-monitor brand selling slide-on second screens for laptops (Duex and Trio lines), founded by an MIT student; average order value of $340 with orders from $249 to $1,599.

evidence.summary: The brand's own Awin program profile publishes 7%–10% commission on the sale, a 30-day cookie, an extra 10%-off discount code, a full data feed and free US shipping; the recorded rate is the 10% top of the brand's own published range.

The profile states the program is 'Great for: Publishers, Cashback and Loyalty, Discount and Coupon, Directory, Content Creators, Reviewer, Influencers, Bloggers, KOL' and offers review samples and marketing content to partners.
No earnings-cap statement appears on the program profile, so the commission cap is recorded as unknown.

reasons.niche_fit: Slide-on laptop screens are among the most demonstrable desk-setup products a tech creator can film.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand's own profile explicitly recruits content creators, reviewers and influencers and offers samples for review articles.
reasons.compensation: 7%–10% published range on a high $340 average order, with a 30-day cookie; no cap statement, so cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Program contact runs through the Awin profile, which invites partners to ask questions directly; no public email published.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application through Awin; creators are a named target partner type.
reasons.credibility: Established US hardware brand with four Kickstarter/Indiegogo campaigns over $1M each and 100,000+ units sold.

name: Llimink
description: Portable-monitor brand selling lightweight USB-C second screens for laptops (LK14/LK15 and Snap series) through its own store, with free US shipping and a full product data feed for affiliates.

evidence.summary: Llimink's own affiliate page publishes an 8%–10% commission, a 30-day cookie, free shipping and an extra discount code, with sign-up running through UpPromote and no fee to participate; the recorded rate is the 10% top of the brand's own published range.
The page states the program 'is perfect for individuals, brands, influencers, content creators, and publishers' and 'is designed to reward publishers and creators for marketing to their audiences'.
No earnings-cap statement appears on the program page, so the commission cap is recorded as unknown.

reasons.niche_fit: Budget portable monitors are a staple of desk-setup, remote-work and travel-tech videos.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand's own page explicitly recruits influencers and content creators, not just coupon sites.
reasons.compensation: 8%–10% published on the brand's own page with a 30-day cookie; no cap statement, so cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Application is on the brand's own page via UpPromote; no public affiliate email published.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application, free to join, and international partners explicitly welcome.
reasons.credibility: Smaller, younger monitor brand than the category leaders, with its own storefront and a staffed program page.

name: TUSHY
description: US bathroom brand selling modern bidet attachments and accessories (Classic, Spa and Ottoman lines) that clip onto standard toilets, sold direct to consumers.

evidence.summary: LinkClicky's program directory lists TUSHY's affiliate program on the Impact platform at 4% per sale, with hellotushy.com as the brand website.

Shopper's listing quotes a generic 5–10% payout range for TUSHY, which conflicts with LinkClicky's specific 4% Impact listing, so the commission rate is recorded as null; no source states an earnings cap, so the cap is recorded as unknown.

Affiliate agency DMi Partners' case study describes running TUSHY's program on impact.com and deliberately building an influencer portfolio (30+ revenue-driving influencers), showing the program actively works with creators.

reasons.niche_fit: Bidet attachments are a proven, highly demonstrable home-upgrade product for bathroom and home-improvement creators.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program's own agency case study documents a deliberate influencer portfolio inside the Impact program.
reasons.compensation: Rate could not be settled — a specific 4% Impact listing conflicts with a generic 5–10% range — so it is recorded as null; cap unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Application runs through Impact via the directory listing; no public affiliate email was published.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open program on Impact, a major network creators already use.
reasons.credibility: Well-known US DTC bathroom brand with a long-running, professionally managed affiliate program.

name: LUXE Bidet
description: US-based bathroom-hygiene brand founded in 2008 selling non-electric bidet attachments (NEO 120, 185, 320 and NEO Plus) that add bidet function to existing toilets without an outlet.

evidence.summary: LinkClicky's program directory lists LUXE Bidet's affiliate program on CJ Affiliate at 3%–15% per sale; because the published figure is a range, the commission rate is recorded as null with the range documented here.

Sovrn's merchant page describes LUXE Bidet as a U.S.-based bathroom-hygiene brand founded in 2008 specialising in non-electric bidet attachments (NEO series); no earnings-cap statement appears in any source, so the cap is recorded as unknown.

reasons.niche_fit: Budget bidet attachments are easy before/after home content and a long-standing affiliate category.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program is a standard network affiliate program; no creator-specific recruitment was published.
reasons.compensation: Published range of 3%–15% per sale on CJ (recorded as null); no cap statement, so cap stays unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Application runs through CJ Affiliate via the directory listing; no public affiliate email was published.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open program on CJ Affiliate, a major network.
reasons.credibility: Operating since 2008 and one of the best-known US bidet-attachment brands.

name: Only Natural Pet
description: Boulder, Colorado natural pet brand selling raw, dehydrated and grain-free dog and cat food, treats and supplements, made in the USA with holistic, vet-approved formulas.

evidence.summary: Lasso's program page lists Only Natural Pet at 6% per sale with a 45-day cookie, and its join button routes to the CJ Affiliate sign-up (signup.cj.com), identifying CJ as the program's network.

Other affiliate directory listings seen during this research put the program's rate between roughly 3.3% and 8%, which conflicts with the 6% figure above, so the commission rate is recorded as null; no source states an earnings cap, so the cap is recorded as unknown.
The brand's own product pages describe Only Natural Pet as 'Born and bred in Boulder, Colorado' with formulas made in the USA.

opportunity.title: Only Natural Pet Affiliate Program (CJ Affiliate)

reasons.niche_fit: Natural and raw pet food is a core topic for pet nutrition creators, with repeat-purchase products.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program targets pet bloggers and content sites through CJ; no creator-specific perks were published.
reasons.compensation: Rate is disputed across directories (about 3.3%–8%, with 6% and a 45-day cookie in the CJ-linked listing), so it is recorded as null; cap unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Application runs through CJ Affiliate; no public affiliate email was published.
reasons.credibility: Long-running US natural pet brand with national retail distribution.

name: Consider The Dog
description: Online dog-training membership offering video courses and premium training videos for dog owners, sold as a monthly membership.

evidence.summary: The brand's own affiliate page states: 'Our affiliates through Impact earn 10% from each referral, not only for the first purchase, but for the first 12 purchases by each new customer' — i.e. 10% commission on up to 12 months of a referred member's payments, tracked by cookie-linked accounts.
No earnings-cap statement appears on the program page, so the commission cap is recorded as unknown.

reasons.niche_fit: Dog-training education is evergreen content for training and behaviour creators, though it is a service rather than a physical product.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program is an open Impact affiliate program described on the brand's own site; no creator-specific perks were published.
reasons.compensation: 10% on each of a referred customer's first 12 purchases — effectively a year of recurring commission per referral; cap unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Program details and sign-up route are on the brand's own affiliate page via Impact; no public email published.
reasons.credibility: Niche, specialist training brand — smaller and less widely known than the pet-food names in this group.
